Shrine bullet resist is listed as both 20% and 10% on the wiki, so it's left out.
tldr: 6 vs 6. Destroy the enemy Patron (the big boss in their base) to win.
Souls are your money and your experience: they buy items and level up your abilities.
Kill troopers, then shoot the glowing orb they drop to secure the souls.
Towers must fall in order: Guardian → Walker → Base Guardians → Shrines → Patron.
Respawns start at seconds and grow to 90s — late-game deaths decide matches.

chain.name: Lane Guardian
facts: Takes +50% less damage at 0:00, shrinking to −50% (extra damage) at 12:00.

chain.name: Walker
facts: Only damageable after that lane's Guardian is gone.
Has backdoor protection: 65% less damage taken and 65 HP/s regen.
Destroying one gives 3675 souls and an extra item slot to everyone on the team.

chain.name: Base Guardians
facts: Killing them gives your team faster ziplines in that lane.

chain.name: Shrines
facts: Invulnerable until one pair of Base Guardians falls.
Killing one turns your troopers in that lane into Super Troopers.
When both are down, the enemy Patron can be damaged.

chain.name: Patron
facts: Unkillable until both Shrines are destroyed.
At half HP it turns into the Weakened Patron: only damageable from inside its pit, and resistant when defenders stand in the pit.

sections.title: Souls: your economy
points: Souls do two jobs: buy items at shops, and level you up so you can upgrade abilities.
When a trooper dies to your last hit, a soul orb pops out. Shoot it to secure the full value; the enemy can shoot it first to deny you.
Other soul sources: Haunts (jungle camps), crates, Sinner's Sacrifice, the Soul Urn, the Rift, Guardians and Walkers, and hero kills.
The team that's behind gets comeback help: more souls from non-hero sources (up to +30%) and faster orb securing in Haunts.

sections.title: Your kit
points: Every hero has a gun and 4 abilities. The 4th is the ultimate.
Melee: light and heavy. Heavy melee breaks Tough Crates, Rejuvenator crystals and claims powerups.
Parry counters an enemy's melee. Since Sep 29, parrying objectives no longer resets your parry cooldown.
Stamina powers dashes and climbing. Out of stamina = no escape, so keep one dash in reserve.

sections.title: Getting around the map
points: 3 lanes. Ziplines carry you quickly from base out to each lane — use them to get back after dying.
Steam Vents: standing on one makes you invisible, heals you, and gives +150% stamina regen.
Cosmic Veils are one-way walls of mist at juke rooms and under arches: you can't see enemies on the far (grey) side.
Healing Snacks are hidden around the map and heal 14% max HP.
Bell Tower: hitting things there rings a bell everyone hears (with a minimap ping).

sections.title: Neutral objectives
points: Haunts: jungle camps in three tiers that spawn at 2:00, 5:00 and 8:00.
Soul Urn (from 10:00): carry it across the map for big team souls and 4 permanent buffs.
Mid-Boss: in the middle pit. Killing it drops 3 Rejuvenator crystals — each heavy-melee gives your team one free revive (3 min, revive at full HP after 3s).
Unstable Rift (from ~11:00): capture point that spawns Rift Troopers for the winner.

sections.title: Dying
points: Respawn time grows with the match: 8s at 5:00, 38s at 20:00, 70s at 30:00, 85s at 40:00, max 90s.
The Match Timeline tab shows the current respawn time with the timer running.
Dying to troopers or towers with no enemy hero involved adds 10s.

firstMatches: Play an Easy hero from the Heroes tab (filter: Beginner-friendly).
Buy the most common early items from the hero's 'What players buy' list — don't theorycraft yet.
Focus on one skill per match: orb securing, then map awareness, then objective timings.
Keep this screen on the Match Timeline tab and press Start when the match clock starts.
